Correct	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6. The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 80.86.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll. Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6. The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 2.00.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect

Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 16.50.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect

font-weight: bold;">&chi;<sup>2</sup> = 3.143</td></tr></tfoot></table><p>You roll a six-sided die 168 times. The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 3.14.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 3.38.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 7.50.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 15.04.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 13.45.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

Correct	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6. font-weight: bold;">&chi;<sup>2</sup> = 34.556</td></tr></tfoot></table><p>You roll a six-sided die 108 times. The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 34.56.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 19.00.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 5.75.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect

Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 6.13.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 4.21.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 14.17.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 1.38.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 32.55.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 4.62.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect

font-weight: bold;">&chi;<sup>2</sup> = 5.636</td></tr></tfoot></table><p>You roll a six-sided die 66 times. The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 5.64.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 64.89.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 3.43.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 23.20.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 30.70.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 1.75.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect

font-weight: bold;">&chi;<sup>2</sup> = 11.000</td></tr></tfoot></table><p>You roll a six-sided die 60 times. The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 11.00.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 8.33.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect

The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 19.83.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces. The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 73.25.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	Fail to reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect

font-weight: bold;">&chi;<sup>2</sup> = 28.643</td></tr></tfoot></table><p>You roll a six-sided die 168 times. The <span style="color: #0247fe;">null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 28.64.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at a <span style='color: #8601af;'>level of significance (&alpha;)</span> of 0.05?</p>	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span>; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The <span style='color: #0247fe;'>null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>)</span> is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.
